name: India
description: India faces high water stress, with large parts of the country experiencing water shortages, declining groundwater levels and increasing demand from a growing population.

name: South Africa
description: South Africa contends with acute rainfall variability, severe regional droughts, and critical infrastructure stress across major municipal catchments.

name: United States
description: The American Southwest faces a historic 23-year megadrought, with the Colorado River and Lake Mead storage dropping to unprecedented lows.

name: Yemen
description: Yemen faces one of the world's most catastrophic water emergencies, with groundwater in the Sana'a basin depleted faster than it naturally recharges.

name: Jordan
description: Jordan is one of the world's driest countries, where municipal tap water flows only once a week for 12 to 24 hours per household.

name: Chad
description: Lake Chad has shrunk by approximately 90% since the 1960s, severely destabilizing agriculture and fishing for over 30 million people.

name: Egypt
description: Egypt relies on the River Nile for 97% of its renewable water, facing severe per capita deficits under rapid demographic expansion.

name: Saudi Arabia
description: With virtually zero permanent surface rivers, Saudi Arabia depends heavily on energy-intensive desalination and non-renewable deep fossil aquifers.

name: Spain
description: Southern Spain and Catalonia contend with record-breaking multi-year drought, with reservoir levels triggering emergency agricultural water curbs.

name: Chile
description: Central Chile has endured an unprecedented 14-year megadrought, forcing rural communities to depend on emergency municipal water tankers.

name: Australia
description: The driest inhabited continent on Earth faces extreme climate-driven boom-and-bust hydrology across the Murray-Darling river system.

name: China
description: Northern China holds 46% of the national population but only 19% of freshwater, requiring the massive South-to-North Water Transfer Project.

name: Brazil
description: While holding 12% of the world's surface freshwater via the Amazon, Brazil's southeastern urban centers face recurring dry-season rationing.

name: Germany
description: Historically water-secure, Germany is seeing declining groundwater levels and summer Rhine river navigation restrictions caused by heatwaves.
